scenarios.name: healthy_chiller_at_baseline
scenarios.description: The shipped-placeholder baseline evaluated at its own conditions: 50% load, 30 °C condenser water, 6 °C chilled water gives an expected 0.585 kW/ton and an allowance of 0.6435. The machine draws 299.52 kW for 512 tons — exactly 0.585 kW/ton — and is silent. All numbers are placeholder-relative; a host that has fitted its own coefficients gets a different line.

scenarios.name: degraded_chiller_alarms_at_60_min
scenarios.description: 358.4 kW for 512 tons is 0.70 kW/ton against a 0.6435 allowance — roughly the 0.1 kW/ton the reference calls 15% excess. delayOnInit holds the condition from the first tick, so the alarm lands at exactly alarm_delay.

scenarios.name: measured_exactly_at_the_allowance
scenarios.description: Boundary, bit-exact: 329.472 / 512 is the same double the graph computes for 1.1 × expected, because the divisor is a power of two and the numerator is that allowance scaled by it. Reals.Greater is strict, so a chiller sitting exactly on the allowance reads healthy.

scenarios.name: measured_just_above_the_allowance
scenarios.description: Boundary from above: 329.984 kW is 0.001 kW/ton past the allowance and alarms on the normal schedule.

scenarios.name: measured_just_below_the_allowance
scenarios.description: Boundary from below: 328.96 kW is 0.001 kW/ton short of the allowance and never alarms.

scenarios.name: same_kw_per_ton_is_a_fault_on_cool_condenser_water
scenarios.description: 337.92 kW / 512 tons = 0.66 kW/ton at 30 °C condenser water, where the allowance is 0.6435. Fault. The companion scenario feeds the identical power and tonnage at 35 °C and reads healthy — the verdict is decided by the regressors, not by the quotient.

scenarios.name: same_kw_per_ton_is_healthy_on_warm_condenser_water
scenarios.description: The same 0.66 kW/ton at 35 °C condenser water, where the placeholder line expects 0.635 and allows 0.6985. Silent. Five degrees of condenser lift is worth 0.05 kW/ton on this line, which is half the reference's own 0.1 kW/ton degradation yardstick.

scenarios.name: raised_chwst_tightens_the_allowance
scenarios.description: The third regressor, and the one whose placeholder coefficient is negative: at a 10 °C chilled water supply temperature the machine has less lift to do, so the line expects 0.525 and allows 0.5775. 307.2 kW / 512 tons = 0.60 kW/ton is a fault here.

scenarios.name: same_kw_per_ton_is_healthy_at_a_colder_chwst
scenarios.description: The companion: the identical 0.60 kW/ton at a 6 °C supply temperature, where the allowance is 0.6435. Silent. A plant that has raised its CHWST for the reset savings this chapter's CHW-0002 is about is held to a tighter efficiency line by this rule, which is the physics and not an interaction between the two rules.

scenarios.name: low_load_is_not_evaluated
scenarios.description: The reference's min_chiller_load gate: 20% load with a grossly degraded 0.70 kW/ton. yLoadOk is false, so the verdict is NO_EVAL rather than healthy — a lightly loaded chiller is inefficient on physics, and the reference declines to call that a fault.

scenarios.name: load_exactly_at_the_evaluability_floor
scenarios.description: Boundary: load is exactly min_chiller_load (30%). Reals.GreaterThreshold is strict, so exactly-at-the-floor is NO_EVAL.

scenarios.name: load_just_below_the_evaluability_floor
scenarios.description: 29.9% load: still NO_EVAL, with the same degraded quotient.

scenarios.name: load_just_above_the_evaluability_floor
scenarios.description: 30.1% load: evaluable. The load regressor moves the expected line with it (0.5353 expected, 0.5888 allowed at these conditions), and 0.70 kW/ton clears that too, so the alarm lands at exactly alarm_delay.

scenarios.name: zero_tons_holds_the_quotient_down
scenarios.description: The divide guard doing its job: a tonnage signal that has gone to zero while the meter still reads 299.52 kW. The quotient is +inf and the comparison against the allowance is true, so without yTonsOk gating the AND chain this would be a permanent alarm on a dead sensor. yTonsOk is false and yFault stays down.

scenarios.name: tons_exactly_at_the_divide_floor
scenarios.description: Boundary on the guard: tonnage exactly at min_chiller_tons (10 tons). Strict GreaterThreshold again, so exactly-at-the-floor is NO_EVAL.

scenarios.name: tons_just_above_the_divide_floor_still_alarms
scenarios.description: The guard's documented limit: 10.1 tons against 20 kW is 1.98 kW/ton, three times any plausible allowance, and the rule alarms. The floor only guards the neighbourhood of zero — a tonnage signal that has collapsed to a small non-zero value produces a believable-looking division and a false alarm. Set min_chiller_tons from the machine's real minimum output, not from zero.

scenarios.name: degradation_starts_mid_run
scenarios.description: A healthy machine loses efficiency at t = 1800 s — a condenser tube bundle fouling far faster than it would in life, standing in for the slow version. The alarm lands at exactly 5400 s: mid-run rising edges carry the same T + delayTime arithmetic as the init case.

scenarios.name: degradation_clears_after_service
scenarios.description: Recovery: the alarm asserts at 3600 s and the tubes are cleaned at t = 5400 s. TrueDelay passes the falling edge with no delay, so yFault drops on that tick and the accumulated time is discarded.

scenarios.name: tons_signal_drops_after_alarm
scenarios.description: The evaluability release, and the reason to read both outputs: an alarming chiller loses its tonnage signal at t = 5400 s. yFault falls on that tick exactly as it does in degradation_clears_after_service, and only yTonsOk distinguishes a cleaned condenser from a dead flow meter.

scenarios.name: load_drops_after_alarm
scenarios.description: The other evaluability release: an alarming chiller unloads to 20% at t = 5400 s with its power and tonnage unchanged. yFault and yLoadOk fall on the same tick, and the falling edge of yFault alone is indistinguishable from a repair.

scenarios.name: intermittent_degradation_never_alarms
scenarios.description: Power alternating between 0.70 and 0.585 kW/ton every 1200 s — a machine hunting between compressor stages, or a tonnage calculation that jumps with flow noise. No single episode reaches alarm_delay, so nothing fires. Persistence is not averaging, and a chiller spending half its hours above the line is a real finding this rule cannot make.
